title: The supervisor keepalive, inside a real Electron app
why: sidecar-keepalive-harness.mjs proved keepalive.ts against the real binary but supplied its own sockets and lifecycle. The supervisor wiring was covered only by source-reading tests. This runs the real app and closes the workspace, which is the action that used to kill the sidecar.

isolation.note: the developer instance and %APPDATA%/jp-study-app are untouched

B.why: A close that dropped no client would make phase C vacuous, and a close that dropped the keepalive too would mean the renderer had evicted it via a shared id (rule 1).

connectionLinesDuringHold: 2026-07-31 12:39:39 |INF| ws > Monitoring connection as desktop sidecar
C.controlNote: The module harness measured the unfixed process exiting after 14,268 ms with code 1. Anything under ~15s here would have been dead.

D.why: A new pid or port here is the stale-token failure mode: the renderer would keep the old ones and the player would fail with Unrecoverable HLS error at readyState 0.

E.why: A keepalive released too late would keep the child alive past the app that owned it.

sidecarLogEvidence.note: countdownStarted true with countdownExited false would mean the switch armed and the keepalive reconnected inside the window. Both false is the expected shape.
